lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.11 - A Listen, point, and say.

details:
Listen, point, and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound.
Listen and point shows they match what they hear to the right image. 
Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, clear sounds, and confident repetition.
“I need your help! I want to go on holiday… but… I don’t know where to go! Let’s look at some famous places together. Have you been to any of these places? Where do you want to go on holiday?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.11 - B. Listen and circle.

details: Listen and circle continues checking sound–image connections. Students listen for specific words or details, then show understanding by clearly circling the correct picture or number.
Look for careful listening, accurate choices, clear circling, and neat work in students’ books.
“Can you be a travel agent and help me plan an amazing trip? Let’s listen closely and circle the places we hear. Where will you go next?”

details: Look and write the letters builds writing accuracy and develops spelling, word recognition and careful copying through reading and writing.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.12 - C. Ask and Answer.

details: Ask and answer gives students the opportunity to practice using the target language to ask and respond to simple questions.
Look for use of transport vocabulary and taking turns. Ensure students are using the picture prompts to help them,
“Come on! Let’s be travel buddies. Ask your buddy where to go and how to get there. I heard it’s best to walk around Rome like the Romans did. What do you think?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.12 - D. Write about a tourist attraction in your city. Then ask and answer.

details:
Writing about an attraction develops writing skills by helping students describe a local attraction with accuracy.
Ask and answer helps oral confidence and fluency while practising simple question and answer exchanges.
Look for clear, simple sentences about an attraction, correct spelling, and pairs asking and answering questions with clear responses.

“Holidays are very expensive, and I want to see some famous places now! Are there some places I can go to here? You can help me! Can you write a mini travel guide about your favourite place? Practice asking and answering questions with your friend, then tell me all about it! Wouldn't it be fun to go there together!”
